newsitem.title: FRANCE: France detains two Corsica bombings suspects.
newsitem.headline: France detains two Corsica bombings suspects.

text.p: French police have detained two suspects believed to have bombed seven post offices in southern Corsica, the Mediterranean island rocked by separatist violence, officials said on Thursday.
The Interior Ministry said in a statement that police from the island's capital Ajaccio, acting on instructions from anti-terrorism magistrates in Paris, had detained the two on Wednesday.
The statement, which did not name them, said they were supected of bombing the seven postal offices during the night of September 21, causing only slight damage.
No one claimed responsibility for the attacks.

French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has decreed a crackdown on separatist violence. Guerrillas, blamed for a bombings targeting public buildings and magistrates, have accused him of burying a peace process.
Separatists have waged a persistent but low-level guerrilla campaign for greater autonomy from mainland France for the past two decades.
